verdict.rationale: Vue clearly delivers component-based UIs. Community reports confirm reactive per-component state and single-file components with scoped CSS, and first-party docs describe nested parent/descendant component trees via provide/inject and reuse of the component API through defineCustomElement. Some users find child-to-parent data flow awkward (emit must be re-emitted at each level), which affects ergonomics but does not contradict the capability. Missing for 10: a first-party doc citation explicitly covering component-local state (e.g. ref/reactive inside a component) and props/slots composition basics; most local-state evidence comes from community comments.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build encapsulated components that manage their own local state and compose them into complex UIs

citations.quote: Vue's reactivity API for component state, effects and computed values is more ergonomic than React's.
A parent component can serve as a dependency provider for all its descendants.
Vue supports creating custom elements using exactly the same Vue component APIs via the defineCustomElement method.
